The victim, identified as the wife of a police officer, was reportedly dropped off after the suspects had collected her valuables and emptied her account through electronic transactions.
But the incident would later lead investigators to eight suspects allegedly linked to the operation, with police recovering 21 mobile phones and three laptops, including the victim’s device.
The commissioner of police, Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, disclosed the development on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja, describing how the command used digital investigative technology to trace the transactions and track the stolen phone.
According to Sanusi, the police tracking unit was directed to investigate the incident after the command received a distress call on the same day.
The investigation reportedly involved reconstructing the operation and tracing electronic transactions associated with the victim’s stolen phone.
The police subsequently arrested eight suspects identified as Yunusa Sani, Ismail Mohammed, Abubakar Usman, Haruna Musa, Abdulrazaq Mohammed, Isah Abdulrahman, Isa Abdullahi and Aliyu Shuaibu.
Beyond the recovery of the victim’s phone, the investigation uncovered an alleged method of making stolen devices difficult to trace.
Sanusi said one of the suspects, Haruna Musa, allegedly specialised in electronically altering the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers of stolen phones before they were resold.
The IMEI is a unique identification number assigned to mobile devices and can help identify a phone when it is reported stolen.
The commissioner added that investigators had also tracked and identified alleged receivers of stolen property, suggesting that the investigation extended beyond those accused of carrying out the robbery.
The case is one of three robbery-related developments announced by the command, highlighting the different ways residents can lose their valuables and money to suspected criminals.
In another incident, a woman returning home from work was allegedly attacked by a masked man who threatened her with a knife, took her handbag and used her phone and ATM card to withdraw all the money in her bank accounts.
The suspect, identified as Chibuike Odeh, was arrested at his residence in Daki-Biyu, Jabi District, following an investigation by police operatives.
In a separate operation, two suspected members of an armed robbery syndicate, Jamilu Abdulsalam and Ibrahim Isa Sani, were arrested along the AYA–Nyanya Expressway. Police said three locally made pistols, 17 mobile phones and other items were recovered from them.
For residents, the incidents underscore the potential consequences of boarding unverified vehicles, losing control of their mobile phones and falling victim to criminals who exploit access to banking applications and payment systems.
Sanusi urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities to the police, while assuring that the command would sustain its operations against criminal networks.
The eight suspects arrested in connection with the one-chance incident remain in police custody, along with the recovered exhibits, pending the conclusion of the investigations and their arraignment in court.
